title: Universal Frame Potential Hierarchy in Critical Projected Ensembles
abstract: Local measurements transform a many body wavefunction into a statistical ensemble of conditional quantum states. In chaotic systems, the higher moments of such ensembles diagnose the emergence of quantum state randomness, but their structure at equilibrium quantum criticality is largely unknown. Here we show that the projected ensemble of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid exhibits a universal nonlinear hierarchy of state overlap moments. Remarkably, the leading scaling exponents are independent of the continuously varying Luttinger parameter. Replica boundary conformal field theory reveals a geometric origin: outcome locking combines the active replica swaps into a single collective rotated sector, while intersecting compact replica branes eliminate the leading interaction dependent zero mode contribution. Matrix product state calculations across the interacting XXZ critical phase and direct free fermion calculations independently confirm the interaction independence and nonlinear hierarchy.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how local measurements project a complex many-body wavefunction into statistical ensembles at quantum critical points. The authors derive that the resulting overlap moments follow a universal nonlinear hierarchy whose scaling exponents are surprisingly independent of system parameters like the Luttinger constant. This is achieved by mapping the problem onto Boundary Conformal Field Theory, providing deep structural insights into quantum state randomness.
main_problem: To determine the universal structure of higher overlap moments (frame potentials) within the projected ensemble generated by local measurements on a quantum many-body state at equilibrium quantum criticality.
main_result: The higher overlap moments form a universal nonlinear hierarchy whose leading scaling exponent is independent of the continuously varying Luttinger parameter, suggesting deep underlying universality.
method: The analysis employs advanced Conformal Field Theory (CFT) techniques in replica space, combined with numerical verification using Matrix Product States (MPS) and free fermion calculations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) at quantum criticality, modeled by a compact boson CFT. The results are tested against the XXZ spin chain Hamiltonian in its critical phase.
key_observables: Frame potential scaling exponents ($\Gamma_k$), overlap moments ($F_k(U)$), and conformal weights derived from replica boundary conditions (BC/BU).
important_parameters: Luttinger parameter ($K$), moment order ($k$), system size ($L$), and anisotropy ($\Delta$) of the XXZ chain.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on CFT methods, assuming a low-energy description by the compact boson CFT. The full potential calculation requires determining remaining compact contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate replica geometry (seams, folding) and map the problem to Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) insertions, while other figures show numerical confirmation of scaling laws derived from ratios $R_k$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the moment operator, mapping the problem onto a folded half-cylinder geometry in BCFT, calculating the resulting spectrum via principal angles and monodromy analysis, and finally confirming the universal exponent $\Gamma_k$ using both analytical continuation and numerical simulations on the XXZ chain.
why_interesting: The discovery of parameter-independent scaling exponents ($\Gamma_k$) for higher moments provides a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum criticality in interacting systems, linking local measurements to deep CFT structures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Replica geometry for a single unmeasured interval U. (a) The seam at τ = 0 carries different gluings on U and its measured complement C. (b) Folding turns the seam into a boundary for doubled fields. (c) U carries partial permutation sewing, while outcome locking on C forces replicas in each group to share one measurement record. (d) Mapping to the disk produces boundary condition changing (BCC) insertions ΨCU and ΨUC at the endpoints of U.

FIG. 2. Two complementary tests of distinct predictions. (a) Interacting periodic XXZ data for k = 2, 3 and five anisotropies test the predicted independence of Γk from the Luttinger parameter K across the TLL phase. Dashed lines have the parameter-free CFT slopes −Γk from Eq. (20) and are anchored only in vertical position to the largest size ∆= 0 datum. (b) The free fermion calculation tests the nonlinear hierarchy and conformal distance dependence for k = 2, 3, 4 and L = 200, 300, 400. Solid curves are the parameter-free prediction in Eq. (24). Statistical error bars are shown in both panels.

FIG. 1. Principal-angle geometry of the folded Neumann subspaces for 0 < k < N. The measured-boundary Neumann space VC and the unmeasured-boundary Neumann space VU share the common NN direction c+. Restricting to the three-dimensional subspace span{c+, c−, w−} makes them appear as two planes meeting along VC ∩VU = span{c+}. The section perpendicular to c+ is the nontrivial principal plane Pk,N = span{c−, w−}, where c−∈VC and w−∈VU meet at the principal angle θk,N; equivalently, w−= cos θk,N c−+ sin θk,N n−. The additional 2N −2 directions in VU ∩V ⊥ C are genuine ND/DN mismatch sectors and are not visible in this three-dimensional schematic.
